claims.statement: Bant is one of the five shards of Alara.
claims.notes: Official source IDs were carried forward from the curated Bant packet; live page verification remains recommended before runtime promotion.

claims.statement: Bant's color identity is green, white, and blue, with WUG retained as color-direction metadata only while VM-160 promotes the live expression key as BANT.
claims.notes: WUG is color metadata only. It is not a live expression key, alias, generated top-level key, placement result key, raw-to-key target, or identity.expression_key.

claims.statement: Official Rosewater design commentary identifies White as the central color to Bant.
claims.notes: Design commentary should not be rewritten as in-world Bant doctrine.

claims.statement: Rosewater's Bant article frames Bant as an idealized White-centered utopia made possible by the absence of Black and Red from the shard.
claims.notes: Use as color-pie/design support, not as an in-world quote from Bant residents.

claims.statement: Exalted is the Bant-associated mechanic from the Shards of Alara block.
claims.notes: Exact rules text and card listings should still be live-verified before promotion.

claims.statement: Exalted supports a Bant placement reading of many members concentrating support behind one worthy champion.
claims.notes: This is Vox Mana synthesis from official mechanics and card-supported Bant structure, not official Wizards psychology.

claims.statement: Bant's social structure is strongly associated with sigils, public honor, and earned recognition.
claims.notes: Prefer sigil hierarchy language unless a future pass verifies more detailed caste terminology from primary sources.

claims.statement: Rafiq of the Many is Bant's iconic legendary knight figure and is associated with sigils from all five Bant nations.
claims.notes: Exact flavor text and story passages should be checked live before runtime promotion.

claims.statement: Bant has a confirmed five-nation geography anchored by Valeron, Akrasa, Jhess, Topa, and Eos.
claims.notes: VM-159A upgrades the complete roster from a manual-fill caveat to accepted source-packet geography. Detailed local politics and direct sourcebook quotation remain bounded until quoted primary passages are reviewed.

claims.statement: Jhess, Topa, and Eos are confirmed Bant nations. All three are verified in A Planeswalker's Guide to Alara (Beyer & Helland, 2008): Jhess is the eastern island/coastal nation; Topa and Eos are two of the Inner Three nations of Bant's central savannahs alongside Akrasa.
claims.notes: VM-159A accepts these names for future runtime geography use. Exact primary passage text should still be checked before direct quotation, detailed local politics, or expanded dossier language.

claims.statement: The Great Conduit is a Bant symbolic/geographic anchor associated with Noble Hierarch in the curated packet.
claims.notes: Exact flavor text should be checked live before quoting.

claims.statement: The curated packet supports Rafiq, Jenara, Noble Hierarch, Gwafa Hazid, Stoic Angel, Empyrial Archangel, and Rhox War Monk as Bant-associated figures or card anchors with varying degrees of lore depth.
claims.notes: Do not infer full institutional roles from card association alone.

claims.statement: Asha may be described as Bant's supreme guardian/sacred authority and presider, while the angel-creation mechanism is attributed to a council of archmages rather than to Asha herself.
claims.notes: The founder claim remains explicitly out of bounds: do not present Asha as the sole founder of Bant's caste, sigil, or angel-creation system.

claims.statement: Elspeth's Bant arc may be described as a defining knightly and spiritual chapter, including her training, knighthood, Conflux-era rupture, Sword of Asha handoff, and departure, but not as governing or institution-building on Bant.
claims.notes: Use the confirmed sequence as source-bound support only; do not route Bant through Elspeth governance or institutional authorship.

claims.statement: Conflux reunited Alara's shards and is the main rupture point for Bant's isolated ideal.
claims.notes: Detailed post-Conflux political conditions remain manual-review material.

claims.statement: Post-Phyrexia material may support continuity of Bant identity, Valeron, and Knight-General Rafiq, but does not establish a complete post-invasion political condition in this packet.
claims.notes: Do not promote detailed reconstruction, crisis-of-faith, or institution-compleation claims without direct official source text.

claims.statement: Bant's in-bounds Commander expression includes creature-forward value midrange, enchantress or aura engines, blink and ETB value, exalted single-champion combat, honor-coded voltron, and clean creature-based combo or value lines.
claims.notes: Commander lanes are source-supported project curation, not official lore.

claims.statement: Derevi hard-lock stax, prison-enchantment stacks without creature/community framing, mill or self-mill without communal creature identity, and mass reanimation as primary identity should be suppressed as Bant primary expressions.
claims.notes: This is a placement and Commander guardrail, not a legality statement.

claims.statement: Bant should be separated from Azorius, Selesnya, Simic, Naya, Esper, Grixis, and Jund through Vox Mana expression-level guidance rather than canon diplomacy claims.
claims.notes: Naya is the most important adjacent shard false positive because it shares White and Green.

claims.statement: VM-160 promotes Bant from the VM-159 raw source packet into live placement under expression key BANT, while lore limits remain source-bound.
claims.notes: BANT is the only live expression key. WUG remains color-direction metadata only. Asha-founder claims, Elspeth-governance claims, post-Conflux and post-Phyrexia political detail, named angel-compleation outcomes, and direct-quotation limits remain source-bound.

claims.statement: Mubin's source-bound Conflux sequence may support Bant's many-behind-the-champion pattern: friendship and rivalry with Rafiq, Esper mind-control and paralysis, research that restores the Sword of Asha, Rafiq's Malfegor victory enabled by that discovery, and Mubin's death after failed etherium surgery.
claims.notes: Use Mubin as support context for Bant's communal-champion logic, not as a standalone placement route or card-facing Commander anchor.
